investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T21:35–21:43Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM readiness check.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that are eligible to schedule remote agent pods. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists and preemption cannot help. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") timed out after ~138–143 s without writing any required evidence fields, causing all contract assertions to fail. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity constraint on the remote-agent VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs or other workloads have consumed all allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 affinity-matching nodes, leaving zero capacity for new pods. Preemption is explicitly ruled out by the scheduler ('No preemption victims found'), indicating no lower-priority pods are present to evict.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their labels changed, effective schedulable capacity would drop to zero even if kata.peerpods.io/vm slots were available on other nodes.

TERTIARY — kata-containers or peer-pods node plugin not running or reporting incorrect capacity on the 2 eligible nodes: a device plugin crash or misconfiguration could cause the nodes to advertise 0 kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity even if underlying VM slots exist.

QUATERNARY — resource quota or LimitRange at the namespace level capping kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations below what the pod requests, causing the scheduler to see insufficient resources even when node-level capacity exists.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T21:35–21:43Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the VM readiness check.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the only 2 nodes that are eligible to schedule remote agent pods. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists and preemption cannot help. Because the pod never became Running, the eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885: createAgent with machineType "remote") timed out after ~138–143 s without writing any required evidence fields, causing all contract assertions to fail. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity constraint on the remote-agent VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-19T21:40–21:43Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes had zero capacity to schedule a new kata peer-pod VM, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes failing pod affinity/selector matching. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never received any response, leaving all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the 2 nodes that support peer-pod VMs. The remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector requirements. As a result, every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod during the eval window was rejected as Unschedulable, and preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims were available. The eval runner timed out (~143–150s) waiting for the pod to become schedulable, producing an empty evidence payload and a full contract violation. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods are consuming all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval-provisioned pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at VM capacity. If the affinity configuration is overly restrictive or the eligible node pool has shrunk, this compounds the capacity problem.

Tertiary — cluster node pool under-provisioned or a node went NotReady: if one or both of the kata-capable nodes became unavailable or had their VM resource capacity reduced (e.g., node drain, resource limit change, node failure), the effective schedulable capacity would drop to zero.

Lower confidence — eval concurrency: if multiple eval runs or real workloads were simultaneously requesting remote agent pods, they could collectively exhaust the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota during the eval window. The sequential failure of remote-agent-create (21:38), remote-agent-state (21:40), and remote-agent-runtime (21:43) is consistent with a sustained exhaustion rather than a transient spike.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields with message containing 'hello from aura', the scheduling exhaustion was transient and has self-resolved, weakening the capacity-exhaustion hypothesis.

If kubectl or cluster metrics show that kata.peerpods.io/vm slots were available and unallocated at the time of the failure, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but rather a misconfigured resource request or a scheduler bug.
If the pod affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec was recently changed to exclude nodes that previously matched, the cause would be a configuration drift rather than capacity exhaustion.

If only the eval runner's service account lacked permission to schedule pods with kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, the failure would be an RBAC issue rather than capacity exhaustion — this would be disproved by confirming other workloads successfully scheduled kata peer-pods during the same window.

If the local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) also failed during the same run, the failure scope would be broader than the remote kata scheduling layer, suggesting a more systemic API or auth issue.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated capacity on the cluster before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct 'capacity' failure mode rather than a generic scheduling timeout.
Add a cleanup-verification eval that confirms remote agent pods provisioned by previous eval runs have been fully terminated, catching VM slot leaks before they exhaust capacity.
Add a node-pool health eval that verifies the expected number of kata-capable nodes are Ready and schedulable, alerting when the eligible node count drops below the configured minimum.

Consider adding a latency-bucketed eval that distinguishes between pod scheduling delays (pre-start) and runtime response delays (post-start), so scheduling failures are reported separately from slow agent responses.
